previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted after noticing dark stools and a small amount of bright red blood in the toilet, accompanied by lightheadedness and weakness. Her hemoglobin on admission was 9.7 g/dL, which was higher than her baseline, and remained stable throughout the stay. She had no signs of acute kidney injury or hepatic decompensation. Given her recent extensive negative GI workup and hemodynamic stability, further endoscopic procedures were not performed. She was managed with IV pantoprazole, temporary NPO status, and close monitoring. Her lactulose was adjusted, and diuretics were held pending outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue pantoprazole, resume baseline medications except diuretics, monitor for signs of active bleeding, and complete outpatient lab testing with results to be faxed to her liver specialist.

encephalopathy or decompensation. She was continued on home

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital because you came to the 
emergency room with worsened abdominal pain and were found to 
have acute injury to your kidneys. This was likely due to the 
fact that you had been unable to eat or drink very well for 2 
days. Although your initial urine studies were supsicious for 
infection, the final culture was negative. We gave you fluid and 
your kidney function returned to normal. Your pain was thought 
to be worsening of your chronic abdominal pain, which may be 
partly due to your liver disease, and may be exacerbated by 
chronic constipation. We did an X-ray of your abdomen that did 
not show any obstruction. Because we suspect you may have a 
motility disorder, that impairs the normal movement of your 
bowels, we recommend you follow up with a gastroenterologist 
after your discharge from the hospital.

Please continue to take your lactulose 4 times daily at home. If 
you are not having at least 2 bowel movements daily, use your 
colace, senna, or miralax as needed rather than increasing the 
lactulose frequency. Please follow up with your scheduled 
appointments with Dr. ___ Dr. ___.

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your stay at ___.

 - Your ___ Team
